name: Windsurf
subcategory: AI coding agents and developer workspaces
tagline: Build a VS Code extension that proposes and applies reviewed multi-file patches

pricing.notes: Typical Pro monthly tier; packaging can change rapidly.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Light daily and weekly agent quotas; exact numeric allowance is not published; unlimited inline edits and Tab.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: Daily and weekly quotas; estimated daily messages vary by model: 7-27 Premium Plus, 8-101 Premium, or 47-190 Lightweight.
tiers.notes: Additional usage is charged at the selected model's API price.

tiers.name: Teams
tiers.limits: Same published model-dependent estimated daily ranges as Pro, with team administration.
tiers.notes: Additional usage is charged at the selected model's API price.

tiers.name: Max
tiers.limits: Estimated daily messages: 42-170 Premium Plus, 47-631 Premium, or 291-1,190 Lightweight.
tiers.notes: Additional usage is charged at the selected model's API price.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom ACU allocation, controls and support.

pricing.freeTierCaps: light daily and weekly quotas with no published numeric amount; unlimited inline edits and Tab completion
pricing.billingTerms: current public plans are monthly; legacy annual subscriptions may remain until renewal
pricing.hiddenCosts: Daily and weekly quotas both apply and reset separately; extra usage is model-priced. Existing $15 Pro and $30 Teams customers were explicitly grandfathered, so two customers can pay different prices for the same named plan.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Windsurf, build a VS Code extension that proposes and applies reviewed multi-file patches. The hard boundary is proprietary coding models, agent context, ide integration, and hosted inference, plus frontier models, context infrastructure, and execution safety.
coreLoopDIY: Build a bounded VS Code coding assistant that indexes the current repository, proposes and applies reviewed multi-file patches, runs approved commands, and preserves an auditable session log.
whatYouLose: proprietary coding models, agent context, IDE integration, and hosted inference
moatNotes: frontier models, context infrastructure, and execution safety
ongoingBurden: model changes, indexing, prompt injection, tool permissions, sandboxing, evaluation, telemetry choices, and IDE compatibility
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Windsurf because the UI can be copied, but high-quality code models, context ranking, safe execution, and constant evaluation are the product. The recurring cost buys model changes, indexing, prompt injection, tool permissions, sandboxing, evaluation, telemetry choices, and IDE compatibility, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Continue
priorArt.desc: Active open-source coding-assistant framework for IDEs and multiple model providers.

alternatives.name: Aider
alternatives.desc: It edits the repo from a terminal and commits its own mess.

facts.install: Install with aider-install, pipx or uv, then run it inside a Git repository
facts.engines: Claude, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Gemini, open-weight and local models through LiteLLM-compatible providers
facts.dataFormat: Repository files and Git commits stay local; optional chat and input history is local, while prompts and repository context go to the selected model provider
facts.gapVsPaid: It is terminal-only, without Windsurf's native editor autocomplete, graphical multi-file patch review and integrated browsing workflow.
facts.setupBlocker: Terminal use, a Git repository and an API key or local model runtime

alternatives.name: Cline
alternatives.desc: A code agent in your editor; the model bill is still yours.

facts.install: VS Code or JetBrains extension, or npm-installed CLI
facts.engines: Anthropic Claude, OpenAI GPT, Google Gemini, OpenRouter, Bedrock, Azure, Vertex, Cerebras, Groq, Ollama, LM Studio and OpenAI-compatible endpoints
facts.dataFormat: Code stays in the working repository and task data is stored locally; prompts and selected code context go to the chosen provider unless a local backend is used
facts.gapVsPaid: Its approval-heavy extension workflow is less seamless than Windsurf's editor-native autocomplete and reviewed multi-file patch experience.
facts.setupBlocker: Sign in for Cline inference, bring an API key, or run and configure a local model

alternatives.name: Goose
alternatives.desc: A desktop agent that edits and runs code without pretending the model is free.

facts.engines: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Ollama, OpenRouter, Azure, Bedrock and other providers; ACP can use supported model subscriptions
facts.dataFormat: Code and files stay local; sessions and configuration are stored in Goose application data, while prompts and context go to the selected provider unless local
facts.gapVsPaid: It lacks Windsurf's full editor, inline completion and graphical patch-review workflow.
facts.setupBlocker: A provider subscription, API key or local model must be connected before the agent can work

alternatives.name: Kilo Code
alternatives.desc: One open agent across VS Code, JetBrains and the terminal; inference still has a meter somewhere.

alternatives.name: OpenCode
alternatives.desc: A fast local coding agent with no loyalty to any model vendor.

facts.engines: Dozens of providers through AI SDK and Models.dev, including hosted APIs and local OpenAI-compatible or Ollama-style backends
facts.dataFormat: Source files stay local; credentials are stored under the user's OpenCode data directory and configuration under the config directory, while prompts and context go to the selected provider
facts.gapVsPaid: It is terminal-first and gives up Windsurf's graphical editor, inline completion and visual multi-file patch review.
facts.setupBlocker: Terminal comfort and a provider API key or local model server are required

alternatives.name: Zed
alternatives.desc: A fast open editor with agents built in, not a VS Code costume.

facts.install: Direct desktop download, Homebrew, winget or install script
facts.engines: Zed-hosted models, provider API keys or subscriptions, OpenRouter, Vercel AI Gateway, Bedrock, Ollama, LM Studio, OpenAI-compatible local servers and external ACP agents
facts.dataFormat: Source files stay local; provider keys use the system keychain, while AI prompts and code context go to the selected provider or local model
facts.gapVsPaid: It requires moving to a different editor and is less centered on Windsurf's reviewed multi-file patch and Cascade-style workflow.
facts.setupBlocker: Editor installation is clean; AI needs a Zed account, provider subscription or key, gateway, or local model, and platform hardware support varies

rejectedAlternatives.name: Continue

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Pro plan and a single-repository coding assistant DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Windsurf in an empty repository.
Use TypeScript, Node.js 22, a VS Code extension, SQLite, and one user-supplied model API; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: build a bounded VS Code coding assistant that indexes the current repository, proposes and applies reviewed multi-file patches, runs approved commands, and preserves an auditable session log.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create a VS Code sidebar with chat, selected-code actions, repository search, and a patch preview.
Index only the open repository and respect .gitignore plus a separate assistant ignore file.
Require explicit approval before reading outside the workspace or running any command.
Represent edits as unified diffs with accept, reject, partial apply, undo, and Git status checks.
Capture tool calls, model requests, command output, and patch decisions in a local session log.
Add token and cost estimates, provider errors, cancellation, tests, and an offline data-flow diagram.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out training or reproducing a frontier coding model.
Deliberately leave out unattended command execution outside a sandbox.
Deliberately leave out cloud workspaces, team policy, and enterprise support.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
